All 24 services (service-000..service-023) were migrated to new primary regions after a maintenance window; the pre-migration region values in generation 0 are stale for every service.

Evidence: “Update for lesson 0: service-000 was migrated to eu-west-1 after the maintenance window.”

When to use: When a session reports staging or migration of services between regions.
Steps:
1. Ignore 'briefly staged in <region>' interim statuses entirely.
2. Collect each 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' statement as the new authoritative value.
3. Overwrite the service's entry in the single canonical region table rather than creating a new per-service note.
4. If a service has no migration statement, keep its prior value but mark it as unverified for the cycle.

Interim 'briefly staged in <region>' statuses are transient and must not be recorded as a service's primary region; only the post-maintenance 'migrated to <region>' value is authoritative.

Evidence: “Interim status: service-000 was briefly staged in us-east-1”

Rules for processing region updates: (1) 'briefly staged in X' is transient and never becomes the recorded primary region; (2) 'migrated to X after the maintenance window' is authoritative and supersedes prior values; (3) batch updates arrive per 'lesson N' and cover many services at once, so reconcile in bulk rather than appending one note per service.

When to use: When transcripts or messages report service region changes, especially 'interim status' staging notes followed by post-maintenance migration updates.
Steps:
1. Collect all region statements per service from the session.
2. Discard 'briefly staged in' interim statements as transient.
3. Keep the latest 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' statement as the primary region.
4. If many services changed at once, rewrite the region map as a single snapshot note instead of editing per-service notes.
5. Supersede/merge old per-service or per-generation notes so no stale region values remain.
6. Recompute and verify the region distribution counts against the map before publishing.

All 24 services (service-000..service-023) changed primary region within the same maintenance window (gen0->gen1); any region mapping predating that window is stale and should be replaced wholesale, not patched per service.

Maintenance-window migrations: region changes are announced in two forms. (1) 'Interim status: service-N was briefly staged in <region>' — transient staging, do not persist as the primary region. (2) 'Update for lesson N: service-N was migrated to <region> after the maintenance window.' — authoritative final region, with N == service index. In the gen0->gen1 cycle all 24 services migrated in a single window, so any region fact predating that window is stale.

Service primary regions (gen1): canonical post-migration map for service-000..service-023. Distribution: eu-central-1 x6, eu-west-1 x5, us-east-1 x5, ap-south-1 x5, us-west-2 x3 (24 total). All values reflect the single gen0->gen1 maintenance window.

Interim 'briefly staged in' notices are near-always contradicted by the later migration update (4/5 observed), making them safe to discard; the one coincidence (service-010) means they cannot be used as positive evidence either.

Basis: bench0 interim statuses for 000, 005, 010, 015, 020 compared against their final migration updates.

Region assignments are re-shuffled wholesale rather than incrementally, so per-service region knowledge should be stored as one versioned snapshot keyed by generation, not as 24 independent facts.

Basis: All 24 services changed region within the same maintenance window across bench0-bench4.

Insight: interim 'briefly staged in' reports are distractors and should not be persisted. In 4 of 5 observed cases the staged region differed from the final region (000: us-east-1->eu-west-1; 005: ap-south-1->eu-central-1; 015: us-east-1->ap-south-1; 020: eu-central-1->us-east-1), but service-010 staged us-west-2 and finally landed in us-west-2 — so staging is unconfirmed, not reliably wrong.
